title: arXiv AI papers — Tuesday, 10 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from checkable point-in-time community attention and independent discussion. Citation evidence is limited for this newly announced batch, and no citation counts were used.

sections.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
sections.abstract: The authors present LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model that maps piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensor data into transferable tokens and report improved dexterous manipulation in simulation and real-robot deployments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim a unified, extensible tactile representation that can be plugged into diffusion policies and VLA policies; their abstract reports simulation and real-robot results across multiple hardware platforms.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported sensor coverage is the three named sensor families; transfer to other tactile sensor types is not established by the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 92 upvotes on the 10 Nov Hugging Face Daily Papers page, the largest checkable attention signal among the selected current-batch papers.

sections.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
sections.abstract: Sage-Taiyi tracks evidence, assumptions, and unresolved questions to choose research targets and methods; the paper reports results on an ideation benchmark and five expert-guided scientific collaborations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report first place on all eight Taiyi-Bench metrics (265 tasks drawn from 50 papers across ten disciplines), alongside two external ideation benchmarks and five expert-guided collaborations.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say future work must refine the reasoning repertoire through accumulated research experience and test its reuse across domains; the applied evidence currently includes five collaborations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 52 upvotes on the 10 Nov Hugging Face Daily Papers page, the second-highest selected current-batch signal.

sections.title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
sections.abstract: Reframe combines evidence-aware policy optimization with observation-gated multi-teacher distillation so visual agents learn to use tool-returned observations and recover from deficient tool actions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report gains over Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD across 14 image and video benchmarks, and ablations showing increased observation dependence and tool gain.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparison is benchmark-based and against the named methods; the abstract does not establish performance in live deployments or outside the evaluated visual tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 37 upvotes on the 10 Nov Hugging Face Daily Papers page; its attention signal is below the first two papers but substantially above the other listed papers with page counts.

sections.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
sections.abstract: WorkflowArena evaluates model-authored delegation and executable workflow organization, alongside final deliverable quality, on 145 long-horizon tasks across eight professional domains.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors formalize workflow orchestration as a measurable capability and report that no tested configuration leads across every domain; their controlled subset also suggests workflow choice can affect weaker executors.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is bounded to the benchmark's 145 tasks, eight domains, and nine tested model configurations; the abstract does not establish how the rankings transfer to other workflows or future model versions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper received several independent technical write-ups, including AICoder, ExplainX, and AILog coverage; its cross-list spans language and software engineering. No comparable public vote count was found for this paper.

sections.title: How Many Exposures Does a World Model Need? Learning Unseen Game Mechanics at Test Time
sections.abstract: The authors introduce MechEval and a 35M-parameter world model, WARC, to measure how quickly an agent learns game mechanics from interaction; tests use 69 mechanics across 20 ARC-AGI-3 games.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that WARC reaches at least 80% accuracy on changed cells for four in five held-out mechanics; the WARC-Agent raises the public-game explorer score from 0.15 to 0.46, while the hidden-game leaderboard score is 0.20.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is specific to ARC-AGI-3's 20 games and 69 labeled mechanics; the reported hidden-game score is lower than the public-game result, so broader world-model generalization remains open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 4 upvotes on the 10 Nov Hugging Face Daily Papers page and cross-listing across three core AI categories.

sections.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts
sections.abstract: Controlled experiments find that emulated NVFP4 pretraining can match BF16 validation loss while requiring more exposures to learn rare facts, with the authors' primary readout estimating an approximately 1.2× exposure cost.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that validation loss alone can hide slower acquisition of rare facts and propose measuring rare-fact recall when comparing low-precision training recipes.
sections.unique_caveat: The study uses transformers trained from scratch, emulated 4-bit matrix multiplications, and controlled biographies mixed with web text; production-scale training outcomes are not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The specific rare-fact result received independent technical discussion in ExplainX; the paper also addresses a practical gap in judging low-precision training by loss alone. No public vote or citation count is used for its placement.
